notes: Concealed-damage rules. Each rule fires on a detected region whose class, surface and position match; the flag carries the rule id, the evidence (measured numbers) and a probability that the geometric condition holds given the measurement interval. Thresholds are restoration rules of thumb, not engineering limits; every flag is a prompt to inspect, never a diagnosis.

rules.flag: possible leak above the ceiling (plumbing, roof or upstairs wet room); the ceiling cavity may be wet beyond the visible stain
actions: moisture-map the ceiling around the stain (non-invasive meter, then pin meter)
trace and stop the water source before any repair
rules.rationale: Water travels along joists and boards before it shows; a ceiling stain is the visible end of a wet path above. Restoration practice is to find and stop the source and measure moisture beyond the visible boundary before deciding what to remove.
rules.reference: IICRC S500 Standard for Professional Water Damage Restoration (source control, moisture mapping beyond visible damage)

rules.flag: stain reaches the base of the wall: possible water on the floor wicking up the board, or a leak inside the wall cavity at floor level (insulation, bottom plate and the back of the board may be wet)
actions: moisture-map the wall base and the floor next to it
flood cut if wet: remove board to a horizontal line above the wet line (commonly 0.6 m / 2 ft)
rules.rationale: Gypsum board wicks water by capillary action well above the water line, and the cavity behind dries slowly. Restorers remove board to a line above the highest wet reading (a 'flood cut', usually 2 ft or 4 ft) so the cavity can be dried and inspected.
rules.reference: IICRC S500 (wicking, removal of affected wallboard); FEMA guidance on flood cuts after flooding

rules.flag: stain directly below a window: possible window seal / sill flashing leak
actions: inspect the window perimeter seal and sill; water test (hose test) of the window-wall interface
rules.rationale: The window-to-wall interface is the most frequent water entry point in exterior walls; water entering at the sill runs down inside the wall and shows below the window.
rules.reference: ASTM E2128 Standard Guide for Evaluating Water Leakage of Building Walls

rules.flag: diagonal crack radiating from a door/window corner: possible structural movement (settlement, lintel deflection)
actions: measure and monitor crack width (tell-tale) over weeks
structural engineer assessment if width > 5 mm or growing
rules.rationale: Opening corners concentrate stress; differential movement shows first as diagonal cracks from those corners. Severity is graded by crack width (BRE categories 0-5: <0.1 mm hairline to >25 mm).
rules.reference: BRE Digest 251 Assessment of damage in low-rise buildings

rules.flag: large stained area: material was wet for long enough that hidden mould growth behind the surface is likely
actions: inspect the cavity behind the stain (borescope / small inspection hole)
follow mould remediation practice if growth is found
rules.rationale: Mould can grow on wet cellulose-faced materials within 24-48 h; a large stain indicates prolonged wetting.
rules.reference: IICRC S520 Standard for Professional Mold Remediation

rules.flag: stain on a wall of a wet room: possible plumbing or waterproofing (tanking) failure; mould risk
actions: check supply/waste pipes and shower/bath sealant on the other side of the wall
rules.rationale: Wet rooms are the most frequent internal water source; leaks in them often surface on the shared wall.
rules.reference: IICRC S500 (identifying the water source); IICRC S520
